cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Multilingual ≠ Monolingual – using or knowing several languages.

p.em: Example: Growing up in a multilingual family is a great advantage.

cosy-blockquote.p: Brain ≠ Body – the organ inside the head that controls thought and feeling.

p.em: Example: Learning new skills builds new brain pathways.

cosy-blockquote.p: Young ≠ Old – having lived or existed for only a short time; youthful.

p.em: Example: Active habits keep your mind young.

cosy-blockquote.p: Memory ≠ Forgetfulness – the ability to remember information.

p.em: Example: Language practice improves daily memory.

cosy-blockquote.p: Active ≠ Passive – engaged in action or activity.

p.em: Example: An active mind stays sharp longer.

cosy-blockquote.p: Focus ≠ Distraction – the center of interest or attention.

p.em: Example: Switching tasks requires mental focus.

cosy-blockquote.p: Flexible ≠ Rigid – able to adapt easily to different situations.

p.em: Example: Multilingual speakers have flexible minds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Health ≠ Illness – the state of being free from illness or injury.

p.em: Example: Exercise supports overall brain health.

cosy-blockquote.p: Skill ≠ Inability – the ability to do something well.

p.em: Example: Speaking two languages is a useful skill.

cosy-blockquote.p: Daily ≠ Occasional – done or occurring every day.

p.em: Example: Daily practice builds lasting habits.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Being multilingual keeps your brain active and young.
★ How many languages do you practice every week?

Switching languages improves daily focus and mental flexibility.
★ Do you find it easy or hard to switch between languages?

Regular language learning builds stronger memory skills.
★ What is your favorite memory-training trick?

Keeping an active mind supports long-term mental health.
★ What non-language activities keep your mind active?

Developing a new skill gives confidence in daily conversations.
★ What new skill would you like to learn next year?
